source: The existing global wiring's period-labelled graph. Retain Z^3 translation coordinates rather than identifying them modulo a newly chosen subgroup.
globalObject: For every base port p and a in Z^3, retain (p,a). A source edge of period coordinate d joins (from,a) to (to,a+d). This is a finite presentation of an integer-indexed cover, not an inference of physical infinity from a bounded test.
claim: Restrict this already defined global wire family to wires meeting the edge-five window, keeping their complete P-N-E segments. Whole internal P/E fibres plus all external boundary wire inputs and outputs form an invertible labelled operation.
falsifiers: A physical window cell or port loses its identity under integer-lift coordinates
A completed wire fails to be an actual native same-axis P-N-E passage
A completed edge is absent from an independently generated larger native sector
An output row is omitted, duplicated or altered
An external input can be omitted while all internal output contents remain determined

stateDomains.unrestrictedLiftedSections: Contents can differ on distinct integer translates; external inputs must be supplied.
stateDomains.canonicalPullbacksOfBaseSections: Contents on translates of each base wire agree. Test whether internal views recover the base section and hence determine external values. Do not infer this restriction for arbitrary lifted sections.

completionBoundary: This constructs an open boundary operation, not a closed 80-fibre carrier or an identification of formal comparison packets with native static contents.
discriminant: Unlike reduction to any of the 31 five-sheeted period covers, integer lift coordinates retain all physical window identities. Verify the exact inverse geometry map and do not use projected cell counts as evidence of injectivity.
